question: What is the primary goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.B: To provide free medications for all childhood illnesses
options.C: To increase the birth rate across rural populations
options.D: To ensure healthy pregnancies and safe deliveries for all women

explanation: Safe motherhood initiatives focus specifically on protecting the health and well-being of mothers throughout pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: Why is maternal mortality still high in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Infectious diseases have been completely wiped out
options.B: Pregnant women completely refuse to visit healthcare facilities
options.C: Transport delays, money issues, and a shortage of skilled staff
options.D: There are too many modern hospitals in remote villages

explanation: You've got this! A mix of delayed care-seeking, poor roads and transport, and health system gaps contributes heavily to poor maternal health outcomes in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional pillars of safe motherhood?
explanation: Easy pick! Safe motherhood pillars focus on family planning, antenatal care, clean and safe delivery, and postnatal care—not military service! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of adding family planning to safe motherhood strategies?

options.A: To ensure that families only have male children
options.B: To reduce the workload of nurses in antenatal clinics
options.C: To allow enough time for a mother's body to recover between pregnancies
options.D: To completely stop population growth in developing nations

explanation: Well done! Proper spacing via family planning prevents closely spaced pregnancies, giving the mother's body the vital time it needs to heal and stay strong. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h2)

question: What is a major preventive benefit of routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.D: Giving tetanus toxoid vaccines and iron supplements

explanation: Spot on! ANC visits are crucial for delivering preventive care like immunizations and nutritional supplements to protect both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: A pregnant woman visits the ANC clinic for the first time at 28 weeks. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check her vital signs, screen for infections, and check the baby's well-being
options.B: Schedule her for an elective sterilization procedure
options.C: Discharge her immediately because she came late
options.D: Tell her not to return until she goes into labor

explanation: Great clinical thinking! No matter when a woman starts ANC, your immediate duty as a nurse is to check her baseline status and screen for any pregnancy risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and spot any danger early
options.B: To record the birth weight of the baby
options.C: To measure the mother's daily food intake

explanation: You got it! The partograph gives nurses a clear picture of how labor is going, helping you quickly catch prolonged labor or fetal distress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: Why is having a skilled birth attendant present during delivery so important?

options.B: They can quickly spot and manage emergencies like heavy bleeding
options.C: They guarantee the baby won't cry at birth
options.D: They prevent the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Exactly! Skilled attendants have the training to handle sudden delivery complications and save lives before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: What makes a Comprehensive EmONC center different from a Basic EmONC center?

options.A: Giving routine iron tablets to pregnant women
options.B: Giving health talks during antenatal care
options.C: Performing emergency cesarean sections and blood transfusions

explanation: Correct! Comprehensive emergency obstetric care (CEmONC) includes major surgical procedures like C-sections and blood replacement services. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h5)

question: What should a nurse do when a woman in labor develops a complication too severe for a primary health clinic?

options.A: Quickly arrange a safe transfer to a higher-level facility with CEmONC
options.B: Wait until morning to see if she gets better
options.C: Try to perform surgery right there without proper tools
options.D: Tell the family to take her home for local herbs

explanation: Brilliant! Prompt referral saves lives when your clinic lacks the surgery and blood transfusion resources needed for severe emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h5)

question: When does the highest risk for postpartum hemorrhage and maternal death happen?

options.A: During the fourth month after delivery
options.B: Within the first 48 hours after childbirth

explanation: That's right! The first 48 hours after birth are the most critical window for watching out for sudden, dangerous bleeding and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h6)

question: A new mother complains of a severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain 3 days after birth. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.B: Report these signs immediately as possible postpartum pre-eclampsia
options.C: Tell her to stop breastfeeding until the headache clears
options.D: Reassure her that it is just normal tiredness

explanation: Excellent catch! Headaches, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain after delivery are red flags for late-onset pre-eclampsia that need urgent medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h6)

question: What is the main health benefit of birth spacing for a mother?

options.A: Allows her body enough time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.B: Ensures all her children are the same gender
options.C: Guarantees she will never have morning sickness again
options.D: Eliminates the need for future antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Proper spacing prevents maternal depletion and gets the mother's body ready for a healthy future pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h7)

question: Why is interconception care (care between pregnancies) so important in safe motherhood?

options.A: It improves health and nutrition before the next pregnancy begins
options.B: It only focuses on baby immunizations
options.C: It replaces the need for medical care during pregnancy
options.D: It forces couples to delay having children

explanation: You've got it! Caring for a mother between pregnancies builds up her health, making her stronger and safer before she conceives again. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h7)

question: Who are the best people to involve when mobilizing a local community for safer maternal health?

options.B: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local community groups
options.D: International sports bodies and foreign embassies

explanation: Exactly! Local leaders have a huge influence on community health choices and are key partners in encouraging hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h8)

question: Why should healthcare workers partner with traditional birth attendants (TBAs) instead of chasing them away?

options.A: To replace trained midwives with TBAs
options.B: To encourage them to refer pregnant women to clinics for skilled care
options.C: To let them manage severe bleeding at home
options.D: To train them to perform major village surgeries

explanation: Well reasoned! Since many rural women trust TBAs, working with them helps bridge the gap and guides mothers safely to professional clinic care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h8)
